title: Weighted least-connections balancer replay
scenario: Rebuild worker health (up/down/draining) from a probe log, replay requests through zone-affine weighted least-connections routing (ties: higher weight, then id), and report availability, assignments, peak concurrency and per-zone load.

verified.why_correct: `end > now` keeps only connections that are still open. A connection that ends exactly when a request arrives is closed for that request, as README rule 6 says, so `>` (not `>=`) is right.
It covers exactly the three timestamp formats the README lists, with month/day order for the slash format.

bugs.title: Draining check compares an Enum to a string
bugs.symptom: test_1_worker_states fails: W-08 is 'down' instead of 'draining'. All other workers match, and routing is unchanged because neither state is eligible.
bugs.why: worker.state is a State member, and State.DRAINING == "draining" is False (a plain Enum never equals its value). The skip never fires, so W-08's three failed probes take it down.
hints: W-08 is configured as draining. Why does it end up down?
Look at the check in apply_probes that is meant to skip draining workers.
Compare with the enum: `if worker.state is State.DRAINING:`.
probes: Why didn't routing change, even though W-08's state was different?
What would make `State.DRAINING == "draining"` true, and why might you not want that?

bugs.title: Timeouts counted as passing probes
bugs.old: passing = sum(1 for p in recent if not is_failure(p))
bugs.new: passing = sum(1 for p in recent if p.result != "fail")
bugs.symptom: test_2_availability fails: W-04 and W-08 show 1.0 instead of 0.0. Their only probe in the window is a timeout.
bugs.why: Only `fail` is excluded, so `timeout` probes are counted as passing. The spec, and is_failure() which the state machine uses, treat timeouts as failures.
hints: W-04's only probe in the window is a timeout, yet its availability is 1.0.
Compare how availability decides a probe passed with how apply_probes decides it.
probes: Why did W-04's state stay up even though its last probe failed?
W-05 has two passing probes but availability None. Why is that correct?

bugs.title: Weight dropped from the routing tie-break
bugs.symptom: test_3_assignments fails: R01 goes to W-01 instead of W-04, R02 to W-03, R03 to W-05, and so on. Every move stays inside the same zone, so peak and zone totals don't change.
bugs.why: When loads are equal (for example all idle), the spec gives the request to the higher-weight worker. Without -w.weight in the key, the lowest id wins, so R01 goes to W-01 instead of W-04 and the following choices shift.
hints: Every us-east worker is idle when R01 arrives. Which one does README rule 8 pick?
Look at the sort key in router.pick_worker.
Add `-w.weight` between the load and the id: `(len(w.active) / w.weight, -w.weight, w.worker_id)`.
probes: Why did the per-zone totals and peak stay the same even though many assignments moved?
Why is the weight negated instead of using max()?

bugs.title: Starts counted before ends at the same instant
bugs.why: At equal timestamps the -1 (end) events must come before the +1 (start) events, because a request ending at t does not overlap one starting at t. Sorting by -delta puts starts first and counts back-to-back requests as overlapping.
hints: Several requests end at exactly 10:00:03, when new ones start. Should they overlap?
Look at how peak_in_flight orders events that share a timestamp.
Sort by (time, delta) so -1 comes before +1: `key=lambda e: (e[0], e[1])`.
probes: Why did routing itself handle the same boundary correctly?
Would a plain events.sort() give the right answer here? Why?

bugs.title: served list shared by every worker
bugs.symptom: test_5_zone_served fails: every zone shows a multiple of 19 (e.g. {'ap-south': 171, 'eu-west': 171, 'us-east': 228} in a full-suite run, or 57/57/76 when test_3 runs alone) instead of 6/5/8.
bugs.why: `served = []` at class level is one list shared by every Worker, and served.append() mutates it in place. Every worker holds every routed request, and the list keeps growing each time build_report runs in the same process, so each zone sums a multiple of 19.
hints: Each zone reports a multiple of 19, the total number of routed requests. Why?
Look at where Worker.served is created.
Create the list per instance in __init__: `self.served = []`.
probes: Why does `active` not have the same problem, even though it is also a list?
Why did the mean durations stay right while served was inflated?

bugs.title: Mean duration uses floor division
bugs.why: `//` floors the mean to a whole number before rounding, so 7900/6 becomes 1316 and 8700/8 becomes 1087.
hints: ap-south shows 1316 but the durations average 1316.67. Where is the fraction lost?
Look at the mean in reports.zone_summary.
probes: Why did eu-west come out right with this bug?
Why doesn't round(..., 1) bring the decimal back?

context_qa.q: What order does build_report run things in?
context_qa.a: It loads workers (sorted by id), probes (sorted by time) and requests (sorted by arrival, blank durations skipped). `apply_probes` sets every worker's final state, `route` replays the requests against those states, and then the report is built from worker states, `availability`, the assignments, `peak_in_flight` and `zone_summary`.

context_qa.q: How is a worker's initial state set?
context_qa.a: In `loader.load_workers`, `admin` is trimmed and lower-cased; `draining` gives `State.DRAINING`, anything else `State.UP`. States are members of the `State` enum in models.py, whose values are the strings 'up', 'down' and 'draining'.
True when the probe's (lower-cased) result is `fail` or `timeout`, False otherwise. It is defined in health.py and used by `apply_probes`.

context_qa.q: How does the router track open connections?
context_qa.a: Each Worker has an `active` list of connection end times. Before each request, `release_finished` keeps only end times later than the arrival time; routing appends `arrived_at + duration_ms` to the chosen worker and its request id to `worker.served`.

context_qa.q: Which workers can pick_worker choose from?
context_qa.a: Workers whose state is `State.UP` and whose `len(active)` is below `max_conns`. It uses the ones in the request's zone if there are any, otherwise all eligible workers, and takes the min of a key starting with `len(active) / weight`.
It builds a +1 event at arrival and a -1 event at arrival + duration for every routed request, sorts the events, and keeps a running sum, returning the maximum running value.

context_qa.q: Where do the zone served counts come from?
context_qa.a: `zone_summary` adds `len(worker.served)` for every worker into its zone. The mean durations come separately from the assignments dict and the requests' `duration_ms`.
